introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0560 History 1, June 2023, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). One and a half hours. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers A, B, C and D: decide which answer is correct and mark only one answer for each question (if you mark more than one answer you score zero for that question). Use a soft HB pencil, avoid spending too much time on any one question, and do all rough work in the booklet. Mobile phones are not allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section A, Cameroon Since 1850 (questions 1-25); Section B, Africa Since 1870 (Excluding Cameroon) (questions 26-40); Section C, World Diplomacy Since 1870 (questions 41-50).
incertitudes: Page de garde lue : 0560 HISTORY 1, JUNE 2023, ORDINARY LEVEL, Multiple Choice Question Paper, One and a Half Hours, "Answer ALL the 50 questions" ; les questions vont bien de 1 a 50, en trois sections (A Cameroon Since 1850 : 1-25 ; B Africa Since 1870 Excluding Cameroon : 26-40 ; C World Diplomacy Since 1870 : 41-50).
Aucun choix a faire (toutes les questions sont obligatoires) : regles_choix et groupes laisses vides, conformement au Paper 1. Aucun point imprime ("All questions carry equal marks").
Sujet scanne sans couche texte, lu page par page en image ; filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignores. Aucune figure ni carte dans ce sujet : figures = [].

Aucune cle imprimee et aucun corrige officiel : les reponses sont redigees par le transcripteur a partir de l'historiographie etablie (Cameroun, Afrique, monde depuis 1870) et doivent etre relues par un historien avant mise en avant.

Q14 (La Mise en Valeur) : les options A (exploitation economique) et C (developpement economique) sont quasi synonymes ; question passee en OUVERTE, la reponse visee (exploitation et mise en valeur des ressources de la colonie au profit de la France) figure au corrige.
Q2 (lettre de 1879 a la reine) : les petitions des chefs douala (Akwa, Bell) sont multiples (1879, 1881-1883) ; King Akwa retenu comme auteur de la lettre de 1879, a verifier dans une source.

Q10 (partage provisoire de 1916) : l'accord de 1916 est generalement attribue a Picot (France) et au general Dobell (Grande-Bretagne), Dobell ne figurant pas dans les options ; Lancelot Oliphant retenu par elimination (Milner et Simon sont de 1919, Picot est francais). Reponse incertaine.
Q12 (premier Resident britannique du mandat) : F.H. Ruxton retenu d'apres la tradition des manuels camerounais ; autres noms (Arnett, Murray...) non verifies. Reponse incertaine.
Q13 (fondateur de la Cameroons Welfare Union, 1939) : P.M. Kale retenu d'apres les manuels ; a verifier.
Q21 (plebiscite de 1961) : resultats par division non verifies dans une source ; reponse deduite (Bamenda, Wum et Kumba ont vote pour la reunification) : Nkambe et Victoria. Reponse incertaine.

Q23 (militant de l'UPC dans le gouvernement Ahidjo) : Mayi Matip retenu par elimination (Um Nyobe tue en 1958, Moumie mort en 1960, Ouandie execute en 1971) ; sa participation exacte au gouvernement n'est pas detaillee.
Q19 : A (Southern Cameroons et Republic of Cameroon) retenue ; B (French Cameroon) est une denomination coloniale inexacte en 1961 mais peut etre consideree comme acceptable par certains manuels.

Q38 : Kenya retenu (tentative de coup d'Etat de 1982 echouee, pas de coup reussi) ; Q48 : Austria retenue (neutre depuis 1955) ; Q31 : D retenue (colonies de peuplement). Questions factuelles dont la cle repose sur la lecture usuelle des manuels.
Orthographe imprimee conservee dans les options (ex. Lyttleton, Kings, Malcom X, Koffi Atta Anan, Cassamance).
Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 14.

questions.enonce_markdown: The town of Victoria is significant in Cameroon in the late 1850s because...
questions.corrige_markdown: Victoria (today Limbe) was founded in 1858 by the Baptist missionary Alfred Saker of the Baptist Missionary Society in London, as a settlement for freed slaves and Christian converts, many of whom came from Fernando Po. The German firms (Jantzen and Thormahlen) and the German Botanical Garden belong to the 1870s-1890s, and the Court of Equity was a trade court of the Douala coast, not of Victoria. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The Jantzen and Thormahlen firms provided jobs.
The German planters established the Botanical Garden.
The London Baptist Missionaries resettled freed slaves.
The Court of Equity settled trade disputes.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the Cameroonian coastal ruler who in 1879 sent a letter to the Queen of England requesting for British annexation of Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown: In 1879 the Douala ruler King Akwa wrote to Queen Victoria asking Britain to take over (annex) the Cameroon coast; later petitions of the early 1880s were sent by King Bell and King Akwa together, and Britain did not act in time. King Pass All and Chief Williams were rulers of the Bimbia area, not the Douala kings who wrote the petitions. **Answer: C.**
themes: petitions to britain from cameroon coast

questions.enonce_markdown: The following European firms based along the coast of Cameroon protested against the German annexation of Cameroon **EXCEPT**
questions.corrige_markdown: The British firms (John Holt, R.W. King and the Ambas Bay Company) feared losing their trade under German rule and protested against the annexation. Woermann was a German firm of Hamburg, which supported the German takeover and its flag, so it is the exception. **Answer: A.**
themes: european trade on the cameroon coast

questions.enonce_markdown: Gustav Nachtigal is important in the history of German annexation of Cameroon because ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Nachtigal was sent by the German Chancellor Bismarck as Imperial Commissioner (special envoy) for West Africa. He signed the Germano-Duala Treaty with the Douala kings in July 1884 and proclaimed the German protectorate. The other options do not describe his role. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: he endorsed the Kings' Memorandum of 1884.
he was appointed as a special envoy of the German Government to annex Cameroon.
he brought the Moewe to the Coast of Cameroon.
he was the first German Imperial Representative in Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown: By the early 1880s, the French trading agents were firmly in control of...
questions.corrige_markdown: On the Cameroon coast the trade of Douala was dominated by British and German firms, while the French traders were firmly settled at Malimba, south of Douala. Yaounde was not yet reached by Europeans on the coast trade in the early 1880s. **Answer: C.**
themes: european trade on the cameroon coast

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the German explorers listed below brought the grassfield region of Cameroon under German rule?
questions.corrige_markdown: Dr. Eugen Zintgraff led the expeditions from Buea and the coast to the Grassfields (Bali and the Bamenda area) from 1889, opening the region to German influence and rule. Dominik is linked to the Beti country around Yaounde, and Kund and Tappenbeck to the exploration of the south. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which **important** event caused Douala chiefs to lose their sovereignty to a foreign power in the 1880s?
questions.corrige_markdown: The chiefs lost their sovereignty when the Douala kings (Bell and Akwa) signed the Germano-Duala Treaty on 12 July 1884, which placed their territory under German protection. Nachtigal's arrival only made the signing possible, and the British consul Hewett arrived too late. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The arrival of Nachtigal in Cameroon.
Captain Brooke arrived with treaty forms.
Edward Hewett annexed Victoria for his country.
The signing of the Germano-Duala Treaty.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Anglo-German dispute over Victoria in the 1880s was finally resolved in ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Victoria (Ambas Bay) had been a British-influenced settlement, but after the German annexation of 1884 the dispute was settled in Germany's favour in 1887, when Britain gave up its claim and the territory passed to Germany. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following was a **social** contribution of the German colonial administration in the development of Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown: A social contribution improves the life of the people: schools and hospitals. Roads and railways, the Botanical Garden and plantations are economic contributions, while administrative units and the police are political and administrative ones. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The establishment of schools and hospitals.
The construction of roads and railways.
The establishment of the Botanical Garden and plantations.
The creation of administrative units and a police force.

questions.enonce_markdown: Who among the following was the British official linked to the provisional partition of Cameroon in 1916?
questions.corrige_markdown: The provisional Anglo-French partition of the former German Kamerun was arranged in 1916, during the First World War. Henri Simon (French Colonial Minister) and Alfred Milner (British Colonial Secretary) are linked to the definitive Milner-Simon Declaration of 1919, and Georges Picot is French. By elimination the British official of 1916 is Lancelot Oliphant of the Foreign Office. **Answer: A.**
themes: partition of cameroon after world war one

questions.enonce_markdown: What was common among the following tribes after the First World War in Cameroon: **Mbo, Bakossi, Balong, Bangwa**?
questions.corrige_markdown: These peoples live on both sides of the Anglo-French frontier drawn at the partition of Cameroon after the First World War, so their communities and families were split between British and French Cameroon. **Answer: C.**
themes: partition of cameroon after world war one

choix.texte: They preferred to be under British rule.
They preferred to be under French rule.
They were divided as a result of partition.

questions.enonce_markdown: The **first** British Resident in Cameroon during the Mandate period was...
questions.corrige_markdown: When Britain started to administer its part of the Cameroons as a mandate (from the early 1920s, as part of the Nigerian administration), the first Resident of the Cameroons Province is generally given as F.H. Ruxton. The other names are distractors. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The **first** pressure group, the Cameroon Welfare Union (CWU), in British Cameroon during the Mandate period was formed by ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Cameroons Welfare Union, created in the late 1930s (1939), is considered the first pressure group of British Cameroons and its founder is P.M. Kale. Endeley and Foncha became leaders of later parties (CPNC and KNDP). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The **main** objective of the French policy of **"La Mise en Valeur"** was to ..

*Options as printed:* A) Promote the economic exploitation of French Cameroon.   B) Promote the French use of native customs and institutions.   C) Promote the economic development of French Cameroon.   D) Promote cooperation between the natives and French administrators.
questions.corrige_markdown:
"La Mise en Valeur" (literally "making valuable") was the French policy of exploiting and developing the resources of the colony (plantations, roads, railways, forced labour) mainly for the benefit of France. Options A (economic exploitation) and C (economic development) are close in meaning, which makes the printed question ambiguous.

**Intended answer: A (Promote the economic exploitation of French Cameroon).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: french rule in cameroon under the mandate

questions.enonce_markdown: The following were immediate effects of the Second World War in British Southern Cameroons **EXCEPT**...
questions.corrige_markdown: The rise of nationalism, the change from Mandate to UN Trusteeship (1946) and the creation of the Cameroons Development Corporation (1946) were immediate effects of the war. The quasi-regional status came later, with the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The rise of Southern Cameroonian nationalism.
Southern Cameroons became a Trust Territory of the UNO.
Southern Cameroons acquired a quasi Regional Status.
The creation of the CDC in British Southern Cameroons.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following constitutions granted Southern Cameroons 13 seats in the Eastern House of Assembly in Enugu in 1951?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 gave Southern Cameroons 13 seats in the Eastern House of Assembly at Enugu. The Richards Constitution (1946) came earlier, the Lyttelton Constitution (1954) gave quasi-regional status, and the Clifford Constitution (1922) belongs to the Mandate period. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Agro-industrial corporation that was set up in 1947 to improve on the social and economic wellbeing of Southern Cameroonians was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Cameroons Development Corporation (CDC) took over the former German plantations and started work in 1947 to provide jobs, services and income to the people of Southern Cameroons. The other options are not the agro-industrial corporation of that period. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which month and year was the UPC created in French Cameroon as the first indigenous political party?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Union des Populations du Cameroun (UPC) was founded in April 1948 (10 April 1948) at Douala, with Ruben Um Nyobe as its best-known leader. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The reunification of Cameroon in 1961 was a reunion between...
questions.corrige_markdown: Reunification joined the former British Southern Cameroons to the independent Republic of Cameroon (the former French Cameroon, independent since 1960) on 1 October 1961. Option B names the territory by its old colonial name, which was no longer correct in 1961. West and East Cameroon only appeared after the union. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Southern Cameroons and the Republic of Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which political party did S.T Muna form in West Cameroon as a result of the KNDP crisis of 1965?
questions.corrige_markdown: After the split inside the KNDP in 1965, S.T. Muna and his followers formed the Cameroon United Congress (CUC). The CPNC was Endeley's older party, and the CNU was the single party created in 1966. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Below are pairs of divisions that took part in the UN-organised plebiscite of 1961 in Southern Cameroons. Identify the pair that voted against reunification with former French Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Grassfields divisions of Bamenda and Wum were strongholds of the pro-reunification KNDP, so pairs A and D are wrong. Kumba voted for reunification, which excludes C. The pair Nkambe and Victoria is the one that voted to join Nigeria. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following institutions created by President Ahmadou Ahidjo acted as farmers' bank by providing them with **cheap** loans?
questions.corrige_markdown: FONADER (Fonds National de Developpement Rural) was created under Ahidjo in the early 1970s as a rural development bank giving cheap loans to farmers. HEVECAM (rubber), SOCAPALM (palm oil) and PAMOL (plantations) are agro-industrial companies. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The only UPC activist and nationalist leader to participate in Ahidjo's government formed 1960 to 1982 was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Um Nyobe was killed in 1958, Felix Moumie died in 1960 and Ernest Ouandie was executed in 1971, so none of them could take part in Ahidjo's government. Mayi Matip, a companion of Um Nyobe, is the UPC figure who rallied to the government. **Answer: D.**
themes: upc and french repression in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: The **first** Anglophone Cameroonian to serve as Prime Minister under the Biya administration in the 1990s was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Simon Achidi Achu became Prime Minister in 1992, succeeding the Francophone Sadou Hayatou. Peter Mafany Musonge followed in 1996 and Ephraim Inoni in 2004. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following UN Secretaries General was instrumental in the signing of the **Green Tree Agreement** between Nigeria and Cameroon over the Bakassi Peninsular conflict?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Greentree Agreement of 2006 was reached under the mediation of UN Secretary General Kofi Annan, to put into effect the 2002 judgment of the International Court of Justice on Bakassi. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The two territories not conquered by the Europeans in Africa by 1914 were ....
questions.corrige_markdown: By 1914 only Abyssinia (Ethiopia) and Liberia were independent states in Africa. Rhodesia, Sierra Leone and the Mandika empire were under European control. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **"Joined the colonial race in the 1880s and lost all her colonies as mandated territories after the First World War."** This refers to ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Germany acquired Togoland, Kamerun, German South West Africa and German East Africa from the 1880s and lost all of them after the First World War, when they became League of Nations mandates under Britain, France, Belgium and South Africa. **Answer: A.**
themes: german losses after world war one

questions.enonce_markdown: An African resistance movement that frustrated the colonial ambitions of a European power in the 1890s...
questions.corrige_markdown: Abyssinia, under Emperor Menelik II, defeated the Italian army at Adwa in 1896 and kept its independence. The other resistances were defeated by the Europeans. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Book titled **"The Dual Mandate in British Tropical Africa"** by Frederick Lugard was intended to introduce which colonial policy in Africa?
questions.corrige_markdown: Lord Lugard explained in this book (1922) how Britain should govern its African colonies through the traditional rulers, which is the policy of indirect rule. Assimilation is the French policy. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which among the following was **not** among the four Communes of Senegal, where Assimilation was fully applied?
questions.corrige_markdown: The four Communes of Senegal were Saint-Louis, Goree, Rufisque and Dakar. Casamance is a region of southern Senegal, not one of the four Communes. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The principal colonial interest of the Portuguese was to ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Portuguese wanted above all to settle their own people in Angola and Mozambique and to build settler colonies, rather than to extend the benefits of colonial rule to Africans. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Solve the problem of shortage of colonial administrators.
Extend the benefits of colonial rule to African people.
Facilitate the creation of settler colonies.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the Pan-Africanist who proposed a **'Back to Africa'** movement for all Africans outside the continent.
questions.corrige_markdown: Marcus Garvey, the Jamaican Pan-Africanist leader of the Universal Negro Improvement Association, urged people of African descent to return to Africa. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Germany had the following territories in Africa **EXCEPT**...
questions.corrige_markdown: Tanganyika (part of German East Africa), South West Africa and Togoland were German colonies. Abyssinia stayed independent. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The military Operation launched by the Allied powers to liberate North Africa during the Second World War was code-named ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Operation Torch was the Allied landing in French North Africa (Morocco and Algeria) in November 1942. Sea Lion was the German plan to invade Britain, Desert Storm belongs to the 1991 Gulf War and Barbarossa was the German invasion of the USSR. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these African cities hosted an important Pan-African congress on African soil in 1958?
questions.corrige_markdown: In 1958 Accra, the capital of newly independent Ghana, hosted the All-African Peoples' Conference, organised under Kwame Nkrumah. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In their struggle for independence, African nationalist leaders used the following methods **EXCEPT** ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Nationalists used civil disobedience, rallies and meetings, and newspapers to mobilise people. Bribery was not a method of the nationalist struggle. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Question 37 is based on this statement made by a political leader in South Africa in 1948: **"... the way forward for this country will be the path of separate development for its different peoples."***

Which policy did he implement to separate different races in his country?
questions.corrige_markdown: After the 1948 election the National Party government of South Africa put in place apartheid ("separate development"), a system of racial segregation by law. Indigenat was a French colonial system and Assimilado a Portuguese status. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these African states has **NOT** experienced a military coup since independence?
questions.corrige_markdown: Congo, Nigeria and Ghana have all had successful military coups. In Kenya, the coup attempt of 1982 failed and the government stayed in power. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "The Nigerian rebel leader who was crushed by the Federal forces in 1970 during the Nigerian civil war" was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Lt. Col. Emeka Ojukwu led the secession of Biafra, which was defeated by the Federal forces in January 1970. Gowon led the Federal side. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which country hosted the **first** summit of the African Union in 2002?
questions.corrige_markdown: The African Union replaced the OAU and was launched in 2002 at a summit in Durban, South Africa. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Between 1870 and 1914, European industrialization had led to the following inventions **EXCEPT**...
questions.corrige_markdown: The telegraph, the telephone and the radio were invented or improved in the late 19th century. The Internet is a much later invention. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Bismarck earned the title **"Master of European diplomacy"** in 1882 he brought these two countries in an alliance..
questions.corrige_markdown: In 1882 Bismarck added Italy to the alliance he already had with Austria-Hungary (1879), which formed the Triple Alliance of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Arms competition between Germany and Britain before the First World War was manifested through the building of ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The naval race between Britain and Germany before 1914 was a race to build bigger battleships of the Dreadnought type. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main reason for US entry into the First World War was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The United States entered the war in April 1917 mainly because Germany resumed unrestricted submarine warfare, which sank American ships and killed Americans. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: To punish Germany for her unrestricted submarine warfare.
To assist Britain whom they shared common language and culture.
To provide loans to Allied powers at high interest.
To promote parliamentary democracy in Europe.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the European state that was **recreated** as a result of the First World War.
questions.corrige_markdown: Poland had disappeared from the map at the end of the 18th century and was recreated in 1918. Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia were new states, and Hungary already existed within Austria-Hungary. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What name was given to the agreement signed in 1928 by many nations that denounced war as a means of settling disputes?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Kellogg-Briand Pact (Pact of Paris) of 1928 was signed by many countries which renounced war as an instrument of national policy. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The **immediate** event that sparked off the Second World War of 1939 to 1945 was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939 and Britain and France declared war on Germany two days later. The other events were earlier causes. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Cold War manifested itself in the following countries **EXCEPT**...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Cold War rivalry of the USA and the USSR showed itself in the Congo crisis, in Cuba (1962 missile crisis) and in the Korean War. Austria, occupied after 1945, became a neutral state in 1955 and was not a Cold War battleground in the same sense. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the organ of the United Nations that brings together all members states of the organization?
questions.corrige_markdown: The General Assembly is the organ of the UN in which every member state is represented, with one vote each. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The first African country to host the FIFA World Cup Tournament was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: South Africa hosted the FIFA World Cup in 2010, the first on African soil. **Answer: B.**
